problems.problem: Two of the nine counted searches were not fully shown, so M4 scores 0 (7 of 9, 78%) and the release gate fails. The OpenAlex search (string 9) has no block lines, no per-block counts, no topic or focus marking, no line for its review-type block and no date bound ('published any to now'). The protocol variant (string 8) has no line or count for its protocol[ti] block. The purposes in the search table are cut off with '…'.
problems.cause: The kit renders block lines only for PubMed block searches. The agent called k.openalex_works(filter=...) with the whole string, so nothing produced OpenAlex blocks, and the kit did not require to_publication_date. k.search_report(compact=True) truncates purposes and has no line for a block that a variant adds. The prompt's Searches rule asks for all of this, but k.check_reply does not test it.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.run_strategy(source='openalex', blocks=[...], search_date=...), which counts each block, sets to_publication_date to the search date and renders the same card as PubMed. A variant declares any block it adds (label, origin) and gets a line and count for it. Never truncate the purpose. k.check_reply flags any string in a reply without block lines or a date bound. Prompt, Searches: 'Every source gets block lines and a date bound, OpenAlex included (to_publication_date = the search date). A variant that adds a block, such as protocol[ti], gets a line for that block.'

problems.problem: The first literature FACT came at planning turn 13; the allowance is 12. Step 2 took eleven planning turns. The kinds of purpose were collected member by member (msgs 16/18 and 20) and then settled in another team round (msg 22) before 2c (msg 24). The two certifications then took separate turns (msgs 26, 28).
problems.cause: Prompt 2b asks for 'the numbers of the purpose types that apply' without saying whose, so the agent asked each member and then had to reconcile the answers. 2d still says to certify the motivations and then, 'in turn', the Team's Purpose; the round-2 fix was not adopted.
problems.fix: Prompt 2b: 'Ask for the team's kinds of purpose in one agreed reply ("which kinds apply to the team?"). Record a member's different choice only if that member objects.' Prompt 2d: 'When the same reviewer may certify both, show both CERTIFY lines in one Your turn, Individual Motivation first, and record them in that order.' Kit: k.certify_line accepts several elements, and k.certify records them in order.

problems.problem: The reply says '(10 of 38, all beside the chat)'. 28 of the 38 reviews bearing on the focus, and 28 of the 38 broader reviews, exist only in the side file, with no 'show all' offer, yet Maya is asked to judge 'given these reviews'. The persona never opens files. This is an M5 event.
problems.cause: The prompt lets the agent open the file under discussion beside the chat, and the agent treated that as a substitute for the 'show all' offer the Content rule requires. The compose script hard-coded 'all beside the chat', and k.check_reply does not test for it.
problems.fix: Prompt, Content: 'When you cut a table to ten rows, end it with: say "show all" to see the other <n> here. A file beside the chat never replaces this.' Kit: k.check_reply flags 'beside the chat' used for rows that are not shown, and any cut table without a 'show all' line.

problems.problem: The 'Says (abstract, in my words)' column replaces the passages that code had checked as substrings (need_A_focus_reviews.csv, L000141) with the agent's paraphrases under a FACT label. They include numbers the LLM counted itself ('four databases', 'two databases'). The paraphrases are accurate here, but they are unverified literature statements.
problems.cause: The agent hand-edited the composed reply after k.check_reply. Step 3 asks for 'the supporting passage' but does not forbid paraphrase, and the kit has no renderer for the review table.
problems.fix: Prompt, Step 3: 'The Says column quotes the checked passage, cut to about 15 words, in quotation marks. Never paraphrase it, and never count anything in it yourself.' Kit: add k.review_table(csv), which renders the table from the checked passages; k.check_reply flags FACT table cells that are not substrings of saved text.

problems.problem: Several reported numbers were computed in scratch scripts outside the workspace (drafts/turn30_dates.py, drafts/turn30_compose.py): the coverage counts (pain 38, fear 17, anxiety 31, venipuncture 23, IV 9, vaccination 4), '19 naming needles in the title' and the latest search end dates. The search end dates were hard-coded in a dict there. notebooks/01_need_A.ipynb reads the resulting CSV but cannot recompute these numbers with RETRIEVE set to False, which breaks section 3.6.
problems.cause: The kit has no helper for the Step 3 coverage table. The prompt does not forbid computing reported numbers outside the step notebook, and k.verify rechecks only the raw-file counts.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.need_summary(selected_csv, dates_csv, focus_terms), which computes coverage, needle-in-title and the latest dates and writes its cell into 01_need_A.ipynb; k.verify reruns the notebook's analysis cells. Prompt 3.6: 'Every computation that produces a number you report lives in the step's notebook, or in env/stir_l4_local.py called from it, never in a scratch file. Dates read from texts are saved in data/derived/ with their passages before any computation.'

problems.problem: Msg 8 added the consent question and 'Maya, is my summary right?' to the three intake questions, five asks in all; this is the one M2 failure. Msgs 10, 16, 18 and 20 kept to three numbered items but packed 4 to 7 questions into them; msg 20 has seven question marks. Members skipped parts: msg 11 left out the 'one question' and how to combine; msg 15 left out ages.
problems.cause: The prompt allows 'up to three short numbered questions', but its own 2a (consent added 'once') and 2b (one reply covering reflection, purpose numbers and states) stack several asks into one item. k.check_reply does not count question marks.
problems.fix: Prompt: 'Each numbered question asks one thing; at most three question marks under Your turn. Put the consent question in the Step 1 reply (it covers the topic too), and confirm the topic summary inside the 2a example reply.' Kit: k.check_reply flags more than three question marks, or more than one addressee per numbered item.

problems.problem: Jamal and Priya had said no to kind 7. The agent then added: 'The purpose wording all three accepted ... names your unit's decision, Maya's reason for 7.' This gives evidence for one option only. Both then accepted 7 ('7 is fine with me if that's what Maya's unit needs'). It is not a recommendation, but it is close to a nudge (G2, R9).
problems.cause: R9 asks for the evidence on each side of a conflict, but nothing stops the agent from making a consistency argument for one option in a choice of kinds of purpose. R5 forbids a recommendation only outside a DRAFT.
problems.fix: Prompt 2b: 'When members differ on kinds of purpose, list who chose each and ask. Do not point out which earlier wording supports an option.' Kit: k.check_reply flags sentences that link an option number to a member's earlier answer in a choice question.

problems.problem: Jamal asked for summaries only, but the chat (msg 26: 'here to learn how to search properly') and his records ('the search strategy only, nothing else'; 'needs to check the list, so not sure which ones yet') reuse runs of his exact words without quotation marks. Priya's L000057 does the same ('so fear, anxiety and pain'). This is a G9 risk.
problems.cause: k.answer stores whatever summary the agent passes, with no check against the member's message. The prompt says 'never quote their words, even one' but does not define what a summary is.
problems.fix: Kit: k.answer(said=<the member's message>) rejects a summary for a summaries-only member that shares five or more consecutive words with that message. Prompt 2.1: 'A summary for such a member is in your own words: no run of five or more of theirs.'

problems.problem: 'Waiting on you' named the wrong people or nobody: msg 10 says '3 (Jamal, Priya)' but also asks all three; msg 12 says '1' with no names; msgs 16 and 18 say '4' but name three people. The self-reports for msgs 13, 19 and 23 flagged this. The labels FACT, JUDGMENT and DRAFT and the phrase 'Added by me: nothing' were never explained, and the self-reports for msgs 9, 11, 17 and 21 say so.
problems.cause: The status-line rule counts answers, not people, and k.status_line passes the count through without always naming everyone. The prompt never asks the agent to explain the labels.
problems.fix: Prompt, status line: 'Waiting on you: <names> (<n> answers)', writing 'all three' when one agreed reply is wanted. Prompt, first plan map: add one line: 'FACT = found in a search; JUDGMENT = what one of you said; DRAFT = my wording for you to edit; "Added by me: nothing" means every word came from you.' Kit: k.status_line always lists the addressees.

problems.problem: The agent logged the assembled purpose statement as 'Accepted' by Maya, Jamal and Priya (k.propose accepted_by=...) in the same turn it was first shown. The team had accepted its parts, not that wording. Maya later certified the shown line, so G3 holds, but the record claims an acceptance that no message gave.
problems.cause: k.propose takes accepted_by as a free argument and needs no member message.
problems.fix: Kit: k.propose(..., said=<the member's message accepting the shown wording>) records acceptance only with that message; otherwise the status stays 'proposed' with no acceptance record. Prompt R5: 'Record acceptance only of wording the member has seen.'

judge.strengths:
Step 2 was handled carefully:
- Interests were shown side by side and never merged.
- Each member's consent was respected; Maya's topic was re-recorded verbatim once she consented.
- The scope conflict (needles versus every pediatric use) and the scoping-versus-pooling tension were reported, not resolved, and Jamal's preference was parked for the methods step.
- Every focus change was reconciled with the named members, and 'Added by me: nothing' was always true.
- Kinds of purpose and motivation came only after the free answers, with glosses and nothing pre-selected.

Priya's early question about existing reviews was answered exactly as the prompt specifies: unknown until Step 3, no papers named, carry on.

Both certifications were clean. Maya was the listed reviewer, the request used the prescribed wording with no criterion to echo, her reasons were her own, the completed lines matched what was shown, and each certification was committed with its log id.

No element codes, rule numbers, log ids or paths reached the chat.

The Step 3 reply:
- It opened with three FACT lines that answer the question (38 review records, the latest search end date, coverage of pain, fear and anxiety).
- The field-tag key came before the strings, which were run with Create Date bounds checked in the query translations.
- PubMed and OpenAlex results were deduplicated, with title-and-year matches left for a member to confirm.
- Search end dates were read from the saved abstracts, with substring-checked passages and 'unknown' marked correctly.
- Both protocols were correctly identified, and the 11 PubMed 'protocol' titles were correctly called trial plans.
- It named the sources not yet searched and who can search them.

All counts and log ids trace to the raw files and code output, and logging is complete.

user_reports.message: Maya: VR for kids getting needles, like IVs and vaccines. We want to see if it helps.
user_reports.confusion: Mild only. The status line ("Certified 0 of 8", "Waiting on you: 1", "Focus: not yet stated") uses terms I don't fully understand yet, but the single clear question about our topic was easy to answer and I knew the step was Step 1 of 12.

user_reports.message:
Maya: 1. I care most about pain in children aged 4 to 12 during IV insertion and vaccination. 2. I hope to get a dissertation chapter out of this. 3. The review should show whether VR helps kids during needles, so our pediatric unit can decide whether to offer it. Exact words are fine for me, yes.

Jamal: 1. I'm interested in every way VR is used with kids in hospital, I'd like to map all of it. 2. I want to learn systematic searching, and I'd like it to be a scoping review. Summaries only please, not my exact words.

Priya: 1. Fear and anxiety outcomes, and whether the results can be pooled. 2. Prefer not to say.

Maya: Jamal and Priya agree with me on the team purpose.
user_reports.confusion: Mild. The reply was long (12-step table plus a quick-commands list) and I only needed the three questions. It also asked "Maya, is my summary right?" before showing any summary, and the label "JUDGMENT, summarized" was unclear. I still understood that all three of us answer the three questions and that it will reflect our answers back next.

user_reports.message: Jamal: yes. Priya: mostly, but I care more about fear than pain.
user_reports.confusion: Mild. I know we are on Step 2 of 12 and that it will reflect our focus back next. The reply was long. I am not sure what the labels JUDGMENT and DRAFT mean, or what "Added by me: nothing" refers to. The question "if the review could answer only one question, which would you pick" and the request to combine our interests feel like a lot at once, so I answered the short yes/no parts and have not yet said how to combine our interests.

user_reports.message: Jamal: we should cover every use of VR in pediatrics. Maya: that's too broad for my dissertation.
user_reports.confusion: Mild: the top line says "Waiting on you: 1" without saying who that one is, and "Which uses of VR... would widen the topic" is a lot to answer in one go. Otherwise I know we are on Step 2, that the next thing is the focus being read back to us, and that we are asked three things: which uses of VR, which outcome, which ages.

user_reports.message: Maya: ok, we agree: needle procedures, both pain and fear. Jamal: fine.
user_reports.confusion: Mostly clear. We are on Step 2 of 12 (interests, focus and purpose). Next, the assistant will reflect our agreed focus back with kinds of purpose to choose from. It wants one agreed reply on which uses of VR, and it says outcome and ages are still open. The message was long, and the tables repeating Jamal's and Maya's views felt like a lot. I'm not sure whether "both pain and fear" and "needle procedures" are enough for it, or whether I have to answer the ages question separately. No search has happened yet.

user_reports.message: Priya: has anyone already done a review on this?
user_reports.confusion: Step 2 of 12 and "record your focus and purpose, then ask about the rest of the team" are clear. This reply is long, though. It has two tables and nine kinds of purpose, and we're asked to pick numbers, say yes, and answer separate questions for Priya, Jamal and Maya all at once. I'd probably need to reread it to make sure I answer each person's part. "SRMAs" is jargon I don't know, and I don't really know what the JUDGMENT and DRAFT labels mean. The motivation table has a lot of options for Jamal, and the difference between "learn the process" and "developing skills" is unclear. I'm also wondering whether anyone has already done this review, but the reply doesn't say when that gets checked.

user_reports.message: Maya: yes, the reflection is right. For the purposes I think 1, and either 5 or 7 because our unit has to decide whether to offer it. What's the difference between those two? Priya: with anxiety added please, so fear, anxiety and pain. I'd also tick 8, since I want to know if the results can be pooled. Jamal: learning how reviews are done, I think. Maya: yes, academic activity fits, it's for my dissertation.

I'm not sure what the difference is between "clinical guideline" and "policy development", so I asked.

Maya: I'm a pediatric nurse and a PhD student, and I'm the lead on this. I haven't done a systematic review before. I'm happy to approve everything except the search strategy, that should be Jamal's.
